# macOS paired harness transaction

The `harness-transaction` job in `.github/workflows/darwin-hq-install.yml` runs on a disposable GitHub-hosted Apple Silicon macOS 27 runner. It builds ordinary Machine and a separate Go test overlay. The latter recognizes one reproducible ACP fixture at one fixed pathname and digest, with empty arguments and two fixed adapter/account mappings. The workflow keeps both binaries on the runner.

The normal first-HQ and dedicated pairing flows pin a disposable software owner. Packaged HQ exports and returns each Machine-signed challenge. Identity's typed Swift parser checks the full canonical install or retirement plan before the fixture signs its distinct transcript. For installation, ordinary Machine must first decline the unqualified adapter without spending its approval. The overlay then applies the same plan. Each operation is applied twice and the test checks the original positive receipt stays byte-identical.

A controller running as dedicated HQ invokes the installed sudo rule, launcher and sandbox. For each new OS account it checks the kernel UID/GID on both sockets, verifies the member hello and broker HMAC, and waits for the ACP response and supervisor closure record. The member and broker listeners are local test peers. The test checks the sudo rule, launcher, profile and policy are gone after retirement and both accounts retain their original homes. GitHub discards these fixture accounts and their data with the runner.

A second pass starts HQ through the archived #200 `createHQ` entry point as the dedicated account. It loads the separately packaged #198 Comms plugin through the regular pin-verifying loader. Both archive hashes are checked. The test runs Souls' real entry point from its pinned main source, with one single-lead Soul for each approved mapping. It verifies each assigned UID, HMAC broker receipt, HQ-supervised launch, task offer and idempotent task receipt. After the first Soul stops, the other must answer another prompt. Both final receipts must confirm containment. The test adapter supports check-in only, so the task remains offered.

The #200 archive has an empty plugin catalog. The test constructor supplies the independently pinned #198 catalog, a read-only enrolled status, and a predicate limited to the fixture mappings. The CLI defaults and both releases remain unchanged. A single customer package, real device enrollment, vendor-adapter qualification and physical owner presence remain independent gates. The hosted profile must report `managed-cooperative`.
